newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee sinks to fresh one-month low at close.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee sinks to fresh one-month low at close.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices fell to a fresh one-month low Thursday as an increasingly bearish fundamental outlook prompted commodity funds to liquidate long positions, trading sources said.
With the 1996/97 harvest well underway in top-grower Brazil and beginning in Colombia and Central America, analysts said funds had little incentive to hold onto long positions.
"What we've been seeing is anticipation of better availability of coffee as we move later into the year," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt.
Coffee prices have fallen by nearly eight cents a lb, or seven percent, since the start of the week.
Traders said news Brazil's senate voted to repeal the ICMS export tax on certain commodities, including coffee, also weighed on the market, though the change had been anticipated for some time.

The market got an early boost in the form of speculative short covering, as well as some renewed bargain-hunting from the roasting sector, but producer countries were ready sellers at the highs. Sell stops were activated once the market fell below Wednesday's low of 106.50, dragging December to an intraday floor of 104.90.

Benchmark December futures fell 1.70 cent per lb on the day, to 105.20, their lowest close since August 7. Spot September slid 2.30 cents, to 114.85, as its premium to the deferreds narrowed further a week before the contract is due to expire.
Turnover on the exchange was fairly brisk, at an estimated 11,174 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
